newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Corvinbank, Konzumbank merger on track.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Corvinbank, Konzumbank merger on track.

text.p: The planned merger of Hungary's Corvinbank Rt into Konzumbank Rt, both subsidiaries of state-owned development bank Magyar Fejlesztesi Bank Rt (MFB Rt), is on track, bank officials said on Thursday.

"Shareholders meetings of both banks approved the intention to merge Corvinbank Ipari Fejlesztesi Bank Rt into Konzumbank Kereskedelmi Rt," said Jozsef Keller, MFB's Deputy General Director told a news conference.

He said shareholders of both banks authorised their managements to prepare the merger agreement and the assets balance for the merger. They also mandated them to choose the independent auditor and take all other necessary steps.
The merged new bank, the legal successor of Konzumbank and Corvinbank, will have the same shares as Konzumbank has now, Keller said.
These are series "A" ordinary shares with 35,000 forint face value, series "B" ordinary shares with 100,000 forint face value and series "E" preference shares also with 35,000 forint face value.
Keller said a shareholders' meeting planned for September would be the first general meeting of the merged bank.
Corvinbank is specialised in financing small busuinesses and in factoring, while Konzumbank is a commercial bank, also serving retail clients.
The MFB group also includes a securities house and regional development companies. It offers businesses medium- and long-term loans, collects claims and turns around companies for resale.
